description: Migration diffing engine, migration file generation, and migration runner. Compares current schema AST against a stored snapshot (.doot/schema_snapshot.json), detects changes (new tables, new columns, removed columns, type changes, renamed tables, removed tables), categorizes them as additive or destructive, generates numbered SQL migration files in migrations/ directory, and implements a runner that applies pending migrations using a _doot_migrations tracking table.
steps: Create src/doot/schema_snapshot.nim - Schema snapshot serialization: Define a proc schemaToJson(schema: DootNode): JsonNode that serializes a schema AST (all tables, fields, types, constraints, timestamps flag) to JSON. Define proc jsonToSnapshot(j: JsonNode): seq[TableSnapshot] that deserializes the snapshot. TableSnapshot holds table name, fields (name, type, constraints), hasTimestamps. Define proc saveSnapshot(schema: DootNode, path: string) and proc loadSnapshot(path: string): seq[TableSnapshot]. The snapshot path is .doot/schema_snapshot.json relative to project root.

Create src/doot/migration_diff.nim - Schema diff engine: Define SchemaChange type with variants: AddTable, DropTable, AddColumn, DropColumn, ChangeColumnType, RenameTable. Each carries the relevant info (table name, column name, old/new types). Define proc diffSchema(current: DootNode, previous: seq[TableSnapshot]): seq[SchemaChange] that compares current schema AST against the previous snapshot. Detect: tables in current but not previous = AddTable, tables in previous but not current = DropTable, fields in current table but not previous = AddColumn, fields in previous but not current = DropColumn, same field name but different type = ChangeColumnType. Define proc isDestructive(change: SchemaChange): bool - DropTable, DropColumn, ChangeColumnType are destructive; AddTable, AddColumn are additive.

Create src/doot/migration_gen.nim - Migration file generation: Define proc generateMigrationSQL(change: SchemaChange): string that produces the SQL for a single change. AddTable produces full CREATE TABLE with all fields (using DDL generation from ddl.nim). AddColumn produces ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN. DropColumn produces ALTER TABLE DROP COLUMN (SQLite 3.35+). DropTable produces DROP TABLE. ChangeColumnType uses the recreate-table pattern (create new, copy data, drop old, rename). Define proc generateMigrationFile(changes: seq[SchemaChange], migrationsDir: string, nextNumber: int): string that writes numbered migration file(s) and returns the filename. Migration naming: NNN_description.sql where NNN is zero-padded 3 digits and description is auto-generated from the change (e.g., 'create_posts', 'add_slug_to_posts', 'drop_subtitle_from_posts').

Create src/doot/migration_runner.nim - Migration runner: Define proc ensureMigrationsTable(db: DbConn) that creates _doot_migrations table if not exists (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, filename TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, applied_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))). Define proc getAppliedMigrations(db: DbConn): seq[string] returning filenames already applied. Define proc getPendingMigrations(migrationsDir: string, applied: seq[string]): seq[string] returning migration files not yet applied, sorted by number. Define proc runMigrations(db: DbConn, migrationsDir: string): tuple[applied: int, errors: seq[string]] that applies pending migrations in order, inserting into _doot_migrations on success. If any migration fails, stop immediately (fail-fast) and return the error.

Create tests/test_migrations.nim - Comprehensive tests: Test schema snapshot serialization (round-trip: schema->JSON->snapshot matches original). Test diff engine: adding a new table detected as AddTable, adding a field detected as AddColumn, removing a field detected as DropColumn, changing field type detected as ChangeColumnType, removing a table detected as DropTable. Test isDestructive classification (AddTable/AddColumn are not destructive, Drop*/ChangeType are). Test migration SQL generation: AddTable produces valid CREATE TABLE, AddColumn produces ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN, DropColumn produces ALTER TABLE DROP COLUMN. Test migration file naming (sequential numbering, descriptive suffix). Test migration runner: creates _doot_migrations table, applies pending migrations to actual SQLite DB, skips already-applied migrations, fails fast on SQL error. Use in-memory SQLite and temp directories for file-based tests.
Update doot.nimble to include tests/test_migrations.nim in the test task
acceptance_criteria: Schema snapshot saves all table definitions (name, fields with types and constraints, timestamps) to .doot/schema_snapshot.json as valid JSON
Schema snapshot can be loaded back and produces equivalent TableSnapshot objects
Diff engine detects a new table as AddTable change
Diff engine detects a new field in an existing table as AddColumn
Diff engine detects a removed field as DropColumn
Diff engine detects a field type change as ChangeColumnType
Diff engine detects a removed table as DropTable
AddTable and AddColumn are classified as non-destructive (additive)
DropTable, DropColumn, and ChangeColumnType are classified as destructive
Migration SQL for AddTable produces valid CREATE TABLE statement
Migration SQL for AddColumn produces valid ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN statement
Migration files are numbered sequentially (001_, 002_, etc.) with descriptive names
Migration files are written to the migrations/ directory as plain .sql files
Migration runner applies pending migrations in sequential order
Migration runner fails fast if a migration SQL errors (does not continue to next)

export PATH=/root/.nimble/bin:$PATH && cd /projects/sandbox/Doot && nim c --hints:off -r tests/test_schema.nim
export PATH=/root/.nimble/bin:$PATH && cd /projects/sandbox/Doot && nim c --hints:off -r tests/test_query.nim
findings: All 39 migration tests pass. No warnings in final compilation. The sequtils and strformat imports were unnecessary and removed. Migration runner splits SQL files on semicolons for multi-statement support. ChangeColumnType generates a comment-based migration since SQLite does not support ALTER COLUMN natively. getPendingMigrations uses filename sorting which naturally orders by the zero-padded number prefix.
